neighbours.label: The complement after a negated ability or knowledge predicate (cannot understand, does not know how, isn't able to control, can't tell whether)
fire: Most small children can't grasp why a promise matters.
The sensor cannot distinguish smoke from steam.
Even now, nobody can tell whether the bridge will hold.
We were unable to determine what caused the outage.
A puppy does not know how to behave around strangers.
I couldn't figure out how the lock worked.
Doctors still aren't able to explain why the treatment fails in some patients.
Outsiders cannot judge what the family went through.
quiet: Most small children grasp quickly why a promise matters.
The sensor can distinguish smoke from steam.
Even now, everybody can tell that the bridge will hold.
We were able to determine what caused the outage.
A puppy does not sleep through the night at first.
I didn't open the lock because I had lost the key.
Doctors still haven't published the results of the trial.
Outsiders rarely visit the village in winter.

predictions: Sentences with can't/cannot/unable/does not know followed by a cognitive or control verb reach 0.3-0.65, peaking on that verb or the wh-word after it. The affirmative twins (can distinguish, were able to determine) stay at 0.04-0.15 and negation of non-cognitive actions (does not sleep, didn't open, haven't published) under 0.05.
notes: Probe: 'does not know yet how' 0.603 (peak ' know'), 'cannot understand why' 0.494 (' understand'), 'aren't able to control how' 0.470 (' how'), 'not responsible for' 0.215, "can't predict where" 0.165 (peak ' will', weaker); affirmative 'can understand' 0.145, 'can predict' 0.040, 'did not go' 0.042, "hasn't finished" 0.013, floor 0.008.
